lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
A line is marked 200, 220, 240, 260. What is the interval? What comes after 260?

FEEDBACK
Interval 20; next mark 280.

WATCH FOR
Assuming every number line jumps by ones when marks are tens causes wrong positions.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Draw or describe two number lines: one with interval 5 from 480 to 520, one with interval 100 from 1,000 to 1,500. Place 505 and 1,300 and explain how you found each position.

Write a short reflection naming one step you corrected and why.

teach_steps.example:
WORKED MODEL
On a line marked in tens from 340 to 400, skip-counting by tens lands on 350, 360, 370... Equal jumps of 10.

TRY FIRST
A line is marked 200, 220, 240, 260. What is the interval? What comes after 260?

FEEDBACK
Interval 20; next mark 280.
teach_steps.explain:
Number lines show position. Skip counting moves in equal intervals; the jump size must match the marks.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner choose methods based on place value, quantity and accurate working, rather than guessing digits by shape alone. Keep every step justified.

HOW TO WORK
Read the worked example and name the places, values or distances that carry the method. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. Compare your working with the feedback: did you use the same skill and show your reasoning? If a digit or place is uncertain, identify what would have to be regrouped or counted again. One deliberate, justified revision is more useful than writing a longer answer.
teach_steps.notice: Assuming every number line jumps by ones when marks are tens causes wrong positions. Correct the value or method, not just the appearance of the digits.
